---- MODULE W4Od8m2p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Desks == {"d1", "d2", "d3"}
Ids == {"t1", "t2"}
NONE == "none"
Votes == {"yes", "no"}
Phases == {"idle", "voting", "committed", "aborted"}

VARIABLES durable, acked, phase, prop, votes
vars == <<durable, acked, phase, prop, votes>>

Init ==
    /\ durable = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ prop = [id |-> NONE, desk |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [d \in Desks |-> NONE]

Begin(id, d) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ id \notin durable
    /\ prop' = [id |-> id, desk |-> d]
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ votes' = [x \in Desks |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<durable, acked>>

Vote(d, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ votes[d] = NONE
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<durable, acked, phase, prop>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A d \in Desks : votes[d] = "yes"
    /\ durable' = durable \cup {prop.id}
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, prop, votes>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E d \in Desks : votes[d] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<durable, acked, prop, votes>>

Ack ==
    /\ phase = "committed"
    /\ prop.id \in durable
    /\ prop.id \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {prop.id}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<durable, phase, prop, votes>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ durable = Ids
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Reset ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ prop' = [id |-> NONE, desk |-> NONE]
    /\ votes' = [d \in Desks |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<durable, acked>>

Next ==
    \/ \E id \in Ids, d \in Desks : Begin(id, d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, v \in Votes : Vote(d, v)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Ack
    \/ Reset
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ durable \subseteq Ids
    /\ acked \subseteq Ids
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ prop.id \in Ids \cup {NONE}
    /\ prop.desk \in Desks \cup {NONE}
    /\ votes \in [Desks -> Votes \cup {NONE}]

NoLostAck == acked \subseteq durable

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostAck
nl:
A university course-registration system commits each seat change to a shared
enrollment record using two-phase commit across several registration desks.
A coordinator begins a transaction for a write id on behalf of one desk, then
every desk casts a yes/no vote. A desk may be slow -- it can leave its vote
unset for a while -- but no desk ever fails outright, so a decision is always
eventually reachable. When all desks vote yes the coordinator commits, adding
the write id to the durable record; if any desk votes no the round aborts. Only
after a write is durable does the coordinator acknowledge it back to the caller,
adding the id to the acknowledged set. After a commit or abort the coordinator
resets to idle so the next transaction can begin.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every acknowledged write id is present in the durable record, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

    /\ id \notin launched
    /\ processing' = id
    /\ queue' = queue \ {id}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, launched, rejected>>

    /\ processing # NONE
    /\ processing \notin launched
    /\ launched' = launched \cup {processing}
    /\ processing' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap, rejected>>

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnceLaunched
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker holds pending match requests in a bounded
work queue. Each request has a unique match id. New requests are enqueued only
while the queue holds fewer than the current capacity; when the queue is full
the matchmaker applies backpressure and rejects the request instead. The
capacity is not fixed -- an operator can raise or lower it at runtime as server
load changes. A worker starts launching a queued match by pulling it out of the
queue into a processing slot, and later finishes the launch, which is the
irreversible action of spinning up a real game server. A match that has already
been launched is never re-enqueued and never pulled back into processing.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A launched match id is never simultaneously waiting in the queue or being processed for launch again, so the irreversible launch happens at most once per match.

NEXT Next
INVARIANT HolderAuthorized
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator gives one ground controller at a time a
time-limited lease on a runway. Granting a lease names the owning controller,
bumps the lease generation number, and sets an expiry; a fresh grant also
revokes any control the runway was previously under. While a controller holds a
valid, unexpired lease it may issue runway-control messages, each stamped with
the controller's id and the lease generation in force when it was issued. The
message fabric may reorder or delay these messages, so an old message stamped
with a superseded generation can still be sitting in the inbox after a new lease
has been granted. Delivering a message takes control of the runway only if the
message's generation matches the current lease generation, its controller is the
current owner, and the lease has not expired; stale messages may instead be
discarded. A wall clock ticks forward, and the current holder may release the
runway.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The runway is only ever held by the current lease owner (or by nobody), never by a stale or unauthorized controller.

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm assigns geographic sectors to drones with
time-limited leases. Granting a sector to a drone is allowed only when the
sector is currently free or its previous lease has expired; the grant records
the drone as the sector's owner, sets a fresh expiry, and registers the drone's
belief that it holds the sector, clearing any prior holder's belief for that
sector. A privileged mission admin can override and reassign any sector to any
drone at any time, ignoring the lease, which likewise clears the previous
holder's belief and installs the new one. A clock ticks forward. A drone may
release a sector it owns, and an owner whose lease has expired can be reclaimed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every drone that believes it holds a sector is in fact the single recorded owner of that sector, so the same sector is never allocated to two drones at once.

    /\ held = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ parked = 0

Request(c, op) ==
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[car |-> c, op |-> op, exp |-> reg]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, held, parked>>

DeliverTake(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.op = "take"
    /\ m.exp = reg
    /\ reg > 0
    /\ reg' = reg - 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m.car] = held[m.car] + 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED parked

DeliverReturn(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.op = "ret"
    /\ m.exp = reg
    /\ held[m.car] > 0
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m.car] = held[m.car] - 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED parked

    /\ m.exp # reg
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, held, parked>>

    /\ reg > 0
    /\ reg' = reg - 1
    /\ parked' = parked + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, inbox>>

    /\ parked > 0
    /\ parked' = parked - 1
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, inbox>>

    \/ \E m \in inbox : DeliverTake(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : DeliverReturn(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Drop(m)

NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper coordinates a fixed pool of dispatch credits
that authorize cars to move. Free credits sit in a shared register; each car
holds some credits; a maintenance bay can also park credits offline. A car
requests to take or return a credit by posting a message that snapshots the
register's current value as its compare-and-swap expected value. The dispatch
fabric may reorder and delay these messages, so when a message is finally
delivered the register may have changed. Delivery applies the change only if the
snapshotted expected value still equals the register (a successful CAS): a take
moves one credit from the register into the car, a return moves one credit back.
A message whose expected value no longer matches is dropped. Independently, an
operator can park a free credit into the maintenance bay or unpark it back to
the register.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free credits in the register, plus all credits held by cars, plus all parked credits, always equals the fixed total.

EXTENDS Integers

EMPTY == [surg |-> "none", snap |-> 0]

Surgeries == {"x", "y"}
Clients == {"c1", "c2"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES state, version, pending, notified, crashed
vars == <<state, version, pending, notified, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ state = [s \in Surgeries |-> "open"]
    /\ version = [s \in Surgeries |-> 0]
    /\ pending = [c \in Clients |-> EMPTY]
    /\ notified = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Begin(c, s) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ pending[c].surg = "none"
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = [surg |-> s, snap |-> version[s]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, version, notified, crashed>>

Schedule(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ pending[c].surg # "none"
    /\ LET p == pending[c] IN
        /\ state[p.surg] = "open"
        /\ version[p.surg] = p.snap
        /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p.surg] = "scheduled"]
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![p.surg] = version[p.surg] + 1]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = EMPTY]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<notified, crashed>>

Retry(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ pending[c].surg # "none"
    /\ LET p == pending[c] IN
        (version[p.surg] # p.snap \/ state[p.surg] # "open")
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = EMPTY]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, version, notified, crashed>>

Complete(s) ==
    /\ state[s] = "scheduled"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![s] = "done"]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, notified, crashed>>

Notify(s) ==
    /\ state[s] = "done"
    /\ s \notin notified
    /\ notified' = notified \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, version, pending, crashed>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, version, pending, notified>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ \A c \in Clients : c \in crashed
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Clients, s \in Surgeries : Begin(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Schedule(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Retry(c)
    \/ \E s \in Surgeries : Complete(s)
    \/ \E s \in Surgeries : Notify(s)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Crash(c)
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ state \in [Surgeries -> {"open", "scheduled", "done"}]
    /\ version \in [Surgeries -> 0..2]
    /\ pending \in [Clients -> [surg : Surgeries \cup {"none"}, snap : 0..2]]
    /\ notified \subseteq Surgeries
    /\ crashed \subseteq Clients

NotifyOnlyCompleted == \A s \in notified : state[s] = "done"

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NotifyOnlyCompleted
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler lets scheduling clients book surgeries using
optimistic locking. A client begins by reading a surgery's current version into a
private snapshot. It then tries to schedule the surgery, which succeeds only if
the surgery is still open and its version still equals the snapshot; a successful
schedule bumps the version. If the surgery is no longer open or the version has
moved, the client abandons its snapshot and retries with a fresh read. Once a
surgery is scheduled it can be completed, which also bumps the version. Notifying
the next-of-kin is an irreversible one-shot action performed only on a completed
surgery that has not yet been notified. Any client may crash silently at any
time and simply stops taking part.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A next-of-kin notification is only ever recorded for a surgery that has actually been completed.

nl:
A vending machine network buffers dispense jobs in a bounded work queue shared
across machines. A job is admitted to the queue only while the number of jobs in
the system (queued plus in-flight) is below the current capacity; when the system
is at capacity the network applies backpressure and rejects the job instead. A
queued job is later started, moving it into the in-flight set, and eventually

the capacity limit at runtime, raising or lowering it, but the admin is never
allowed to set the capacity below the number of jobs currently in the system.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of jobs in the system, queued plus in-flight, never exceeds the current capacity.

An airport baggage router manages a fixed fleet of baggage carts. Carts sit
either in the central depot or are leased out to loading zones under time-limited
leases. Leasing a cart to a zone moves one cart from the depot to that zone and
sets a fresh expiry. A clock ticks forward. When a zone's lease expires, all of
that zone's carts are reclaimed back into the depot at once. A privileged router
admin can override the leases and rebalance the fleet directly, moving a cart
from one zone to another regardless of lease state.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of carts across all loading zones plus the number of carts in the depot always equals the fixed fleet size.
